task: JS-161, JS-166, JS-045, JS-060 and the viewer-facing set
brief: The owner asked where the product stands as something viable. docs/status.md: playback is strong; artwork, user management, per-user libraries, Quick Connect, Next Up, the default subtitle and migration are not built; JS-150 to JS-173 went almost entirely to transcode robustness. Options: the order as is; the viewer-facing set after JS-161 and JS-166; the set first; other. (brief-triage-0522.md)
tradeoff: Given up: JS-164, JS-169, JS-170, JS-135, JS-136, JS-148, JS-143, JS-165, JS-056 and JS-057 each wait about ten tasks longer, so an operator waits longer for autoscaling's signal, GPU re-encodes and the x264 preset. Kept: the measured 4K HDR stall is still closed first.
serves: PRODUCT.md, The road there: 'each stage usable on its own', stages 3 (People) and 4 (A living library) before 5; goal 1 for JS-161 and JS-166.
entry: Option (b), amended. JS-161 and JS-166 stay first on the dogfood's measured stall (JS-154). The viewer-facing set then goes ahead of all remaining measurement, tuning, GPU and autoscaling work, in the road's order: JS-041, JS-127, JS-033, JS-036, JS-037, JS-045, JS-047, JS-060 at 25 to 32, then JS-157 and JS-150; JS-164, JS-169, JS-170 and the rest follow at 35 to 51 with their content unchanged. JS-045 and JS-060 gain two criteria each. The lead's estimate that this set makes a household viable is unverified and is not a milestone. Reopens on: JS-166 leaving the stall open or dogfood refusals after JS-161 (JS-169 and JS-164 return to directly after JS-166); a week's dogfood count of requests answered 404 or by a stub, by route (reorders the set); a second household waiting (JS-060 and JS-150 move ahead of JS-045).
